title: Supported integral finite models: the actual restriction is the inverse-limit finite-level arrow
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps, also for $\Omega$. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that for every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, without a common annihilator, the actual restriction $H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\to H^q((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$ is bijective for every $q\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Choose a finite chain
$$S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}T_{r-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0'=T,$$
where each arrow is either a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $J_k=(a_k)_!$ in the open case and $J_k=(a_k)_*$ in the closed case, and put $J=J_1\circ\cdots\circ J_r$, with $J=\mathrm{id}$ for $r=0$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. The symbol $T_0'$ is only the root of this chain; the closed member of the pair is $T_0$.
Let $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ or $R=\mathcal O_E$, and let $\pi$ be $\ell$ in the first case and a uniformizer of $\mathcal O_E$ in the second [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $L$ be an $R_S$-module with a finite constant scalar local model: locally on a pro-étale cover it is $R_U\otimes_{\underline R}\underline P$ for a finitely presented scalar $R$-module $P$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Set $L_n=L/\pi^nL$ for $n\geq1$, with the quotient transition maps. Let $\nu_V:V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}\to V_{\mathrm{et}}$ be site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. There is an inverse system $F_n$ of étale $R/\pi^n$-module sheaves on $T$, unique up to the unique isomorphism respecting the following identifications, with compatible isomorphisms $\nu_T^*F_n\cong J L_n$ and $\nu_{T_0}^*t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F_n\cong t^*J L_n$. Each underlying abelian sheaf $F_n$ is killed by a power of $\ell$.
There is a natural isomorphism of arrows in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$
$$\bigl[R\Gamma(T,J L[0])\xrightarrow{\rho}R\Gamma(T_0,t^*J L[0])\bigr]\ \cong\ R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\bigl[R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},F_n[0])\xrightarrow{\rho_n}R\Gamma((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F_n[0])\bigr].$$
The pro-étale sites are understood on the left. On the right, inverse limit means the total right derived functor on strict inverse systems of complexes of abelian groups [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-derived-limit], applied to both endpoints and the compatible restriction maps. The two horizontal maps are the actual derived restrictions, not freely chosen cohomology identifications. The vertical isomorphisms respect the quotient maps of $L$ and every actual module map between finite models. There is no assertion that an image of a map between finite models is complete or has this presentation. Zero modules, torsion scalar modules, the identity chain, empty schemes, and mixed open/closed chains are included. The original torsion-rigidity hypothesis is retained; no invertibility of $\ell$, Noetherianity, or common annihilator for the test sheaves is added.

proof.text: Construct scalar coordinates directly from the natural endomorphisms scalar(a): verify scalar(1), additivity and multiplication. Install the resulting sectionwise R-action. Forgetting this action is exactly the existing internal-module forgetful functor; it is exact, so the coordinate functor is exact. Grothendieck abelian module and tower categories supply all K-injective resolution instances.

Apply supported_integral_finite_quotients. Construct descent by applying comparisonLowerStar levelwise to the actual supported quotient functor. Classicality makes the comparison counit invertible. Naturality of this counit gives the strict-tower identification. Restriction evaluates the quotient relation and ell-power annihilator on etale objects. Full faithfulness of comparisonUpperStar, also on functor categories, supplies the unique marked natural isomorphism to any other descent.

Construct the pulled-back identification by composing the inverse canonical comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso, upperStar applied to d.identification, and the scalar-coordinate upper comparison. Whiskering and associators make this a natural isomorphism on models and strict towers; evaluating it is exactly the required pullback_normalization.

Apply normalized endpoint reconstruction to get natural endpoint isomorphisms l and r and their augmentation equations. The normalized restriction-square theorem gives l followed by the etale tower restriction equal to integral restriction followed by r. Arrow.isoMk and endpoint naturality assemble a natural isomorphism of arrows. Its left and right projections are definitionally l and r, so the endpoint equations are exactly source_normalization and target_normalization. The torsion-rigidity hypothesis is retained unchanged and is unused here, as intended by the original plan.
